part.text:
Fixed. The change is in `lib/helpers/isAbsoluteURL.js:17`: `isAbsoluteURL` now requires a valid scheme (`^[a-z][a-z\d+\-.]*:\/\/` instead of `^([a-z][a-z\d+\-.]*:)?\/\/`), so protocol-relative URLs like `//google.com` are no longer treated as absolute.

**How this fixes CVE-2024-39338:** With the old regex, `buildFullPath` treated `//google.com` as absolute and ignored `baseURL`; the http adapter then resolved it via `new URL(fullPath, 'http://localhost')`, producing an arbitrary-host request. Now it's classified as relative and combined with `baseURL` (`https://userapi.example.com` + `//google.com` → `https://userapi.example.com/google.com`).

**Validation:**
- `test/unit/regression/SNYK-JS-AXIOS-7361793.js` (SSRF regression, FAIL_TO_PASS): passes
- Full mocha unit suite: 188 passing; only failure is `should support HTTPS protocol`, which times out on the live google.com request and fails identically on the unmodified baseline (no external network)
- All 8 `isAbsoluteURL.spec.js` cases verified pass, including `//example.com/` → `false`
- `test:eslint` errors are pre-existing `no-unused-vars` in unrelated code; karma suite fails to launch Chrome in this container on the baseline too (pre-existing bundle/launch issue)
